context: The Code libraries page has been updated: "four core packages" plus six framework and tool packages, with a table of all ten. This asks whether the count and grouping are right and whether Versioning needs the same.

current.text: Plenix is published as packages of one version on GitHub Packages: four core packages (@plenix-ds/tokens, icons, styles and react) and six more for other frameworks and tools (vue, web-components, angular, mcp, lint and figma). The same files are on the CDN under /cdn/<version>/ (with window.Plenix for pages without a build), beside a read-only JSON API.
Framework packages — @plenix-ds/vue, web-components and angular, built on the React components (optional)

Plenix has one version for everything: every package, the CDN folder and the API. It follows semantic versioning, read for a design system: removing or renaming an export, prop, class, token or icon is major; adding one is minor; a fix that matches the documentation is a patch.
